title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (end of §39). On the previous page Grothendieck is trying to determine the semi-direct product (46). That is an extension of a group M_{0,3} by roots of unity ν, built over the profinite fundamental group π̂_{0,3} of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. M_{0,3} is a group of exterior automorphisms Γ ⊂ Autext_ex(π̂_{0,3}), subject to congruence conditions; it is a candidate for (essentially) the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group.
- Over the subgroup T̂^+_{0,3} ≃ SL(2,Ẑ)^{∧+} the extension is already known.
- The remaining indeterminacy is therefore Ker(Hom(M_{0,3},ν) → Hom(T_{0,3},ν)) ≃ Hom(Γ,ν).
- If Γ^{ab} → Ẑ* (cyclotomic character) is an isomorphism, the indeterminacy is Hom((Ẑ*)_2, ν), which he calls 'big'.

This page opens with the comment that one would need a slightly clever extra element to cut this down. He guesses it is tied to interpreting M_{0,3} as an N'_{1,1}: introducing, inside the 'projective [= profinite/anabelian] theory of rational curves', the 'projective theory of elliptic curves'. In other words, the genus-0 object should be controlled by its genus-1 avatar.

§40 starts a 'paraphrase of Legendre's theory in terms of (topological-isotopic) fundamental groups'. Legendre's theory is the classical correspondence: the curve y² = x(x−1)(x−λ) is a double cover of P^1 branched at 0, 1, λ, ∞. It identifies elliptic curves with full level-2 structure with 4-pointed lines, so the λ-line M_{0,4} = P^1−{0,1,∞} becomes Γ(2)\H. He first wants to treat discrete groups, which he has 'better in hand', before passing to profinite ones.

Definitions on this page:
- C_{0,3}: the groupoid of 'groups with loops' (groupes à lacets) of type (0,3), with the loops 'fléchés' (oriented/marked). Its model object is Π_{0,3} = free group on two generators with three distinguished conjugacy classes of loops. Every object is isomorphic to the model, so C_{0,3} ≃ the category of torsors under Autext(Π_{0,3}) ≃ T_{0,3}, which (49) identifies with a quotient of GL(2,Z).
- C^{cart}_{1,1}: the groupoid of 'cartesian' groups with loops of type (1,1), modelled on Π_{1,1} = ⟨x,y,l | [x,y]l = 1⟩, the once-punctured torus group with its boundary loop l. The next page states that C^{cart}_{1,1} ≃ Tors(Autext(Π_{1,1})) and that Autext(Π_{1,1}) ≃ GL(2,Z), by the action on (Π_{1,1})^{ab} = Z² (Dehn–Nielsen–Baer for the punctured torus).
- The 'Legendre functor' L: C_{1,1} → C_{0,3} is then defined (next page) as change of structure group along the canonical map GL(2,Z) → T_{0,3}. Topologically this means: quotient the punctured torus by the elliptic involution and take the induced loop structure on the sphere with the branch points.

This is the discrete prototype of the profinite comparison he wants: GT acting in genus 1 versus genus 0.
errors: The target group in (49) is unclear as transcribed ('GL(2,Z)^*/±1 ≃ GP(1,Z)'). The rigid (0,3)-structure has a finite exterior automorphism group. That group is the extended mapping class group S_3×{±1} ≅ GL(2,Z)/(Γ(2)∩SL(2,Z)), of order 12. It is reached by reduction mod 2 together with the determinant.

The kernel of the Legendre map, Γ(2)∩SL(2,Z), contains −1, and Γ(2)/±1 ≅ F_2 ≅ Π_{0,3}; this is the λ-line itself. If Grothendieck's 'fléché' structure is a richer structure (e.g. tangential base points), the target could instead be infinite, such as PGL(2,Z). The page alone does not settle this.
The kernel identification (48) ≃ Hom(Γ,ν) and the reduction to Hom((Ẑ*)_2, ν) rest on unproven hypotheses that he states as such ('si on suppose'). There is no error, but there is a gap.

ideas.what: Cut down the indeterminacy of the genus-0 semi-direct product/extension (the GT-type object M_{0,3}) by using the genus-1 interpretation, M_{0,3} viewed as N'_{1,1}.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of GT with genus-one (M_{1,1}, M_{1,2}) mapping class groups; level-2 Legendre link between Γ(2) and π_1(M_{0,4})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1997, 'On a new version of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group'); Nakamura–Schneps; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps; later Enriquez (elliptic associators)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme stresses the role of the modular dimension ≤2 pieces (0,4),(0,5),(1,1),(1,2) of the Teichmüller tower. This specific use to cut down an indeterminacy is not known to me in print.

ideas.what: Groupoids of 'groups with loops' of type (g,n) are equivalent to torsors under the exterior automorphism group of the model group.
ideas.modern_name: Discrete/profinite Teichmüller groupoid; classifying torsors under the extended mapping class group (Dehn–Nielsen–Baer)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated), language of 'groupes à lacets'

ideas.what: Legendre functor: change of group along GL(2,Z) → Autext(Π_{0,3}), i.e. the elliptic involution quotient from the punctured torus to the sphere with branch points.
ideas.modern_name: Legendre family / level-2 structure: M_{1,1}[2] ≅ M_{0,4}, Γ(2)/±1 ≅ π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Legendre/Jacobi classically; in the anabelian/GT setting Nakamura, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps, Ihara
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse mentions the (1,1) and (0,4) relation in passing; this categorical 'Legendre functor' is not known to me in print.

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly anticipates that the residual ambiguity, of size Hom((Ẑ*)_2, ν), in the genus-0 Galois/GT extension should be killed by genus-1 (elliptic, Legendre) considerations. This is the mechanism later realized by the genus-one relations in Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps and in Nakamura–Schneps.
missed.quote: on devine qu'il est lié justement à l'interprétation d'un M_{0,3} comme un N'_{1,1} — i.e. à l'introduction, dans une "théorie projective des courbes rationnelles" de la "théorie projective des courbes elliptiques"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a documented precursor (c. 1981) of the idea that genus-1 compatibility constrains GT. It would also be of historical interest for elliptic associators.

missed.claim: §40 sets up a discrete-then-profinite 'Legendre functor' programme as a tool to settle the indeterminacy; whether the following pages complete it is unknown from this page.
missed.quote: Paraphrase (en termes des groupes fondamentaux topologico-isotopiques) de la théorie de Legendre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The exact torsor-level Legendre comparison could pin down a sign or 2-torsion ambiguity in the GT action, if not already covered by LNS/Nakamura.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics shown is classical (Legendre level-2, Dehn–Nielsen). The interest is historical: an explicit early anticipation that genus-1 structure removes ambiguity in the genus-0 GT-type extension, later developed by others.
transcription_corrections: 'un élément un peu astucieux' is likely right; the word read as 'rétrécissement' plausibly means narrowing the indeterminacy.
§40 title as written: 'Paraphrase (en termes des groupes fondamentaux topologico-isotopiques) de la théorie de Legendre'; 'topologico-isotopiques' is an insertion.
'qu'on a mieux en mains' rather than 'qu'on connaît mieux en mains'.
'C^{cat}_{1,1}' should read C^{cart}_{1,1} ('catégorie des groupes cartésiens'), consistent with C^{ext}/C^{cart} on the next page.
In (49) the right-hand groups are hard to read ('Gl(2,Z)^{*}/±1 ≃ GP(1,Z)?'); mathematically one expects a quotient of GL(2,Z) by a level-2 subgroup.
